integrated_description: Clinicians should disclose diagnostic uncertainty honestly and compassionately, beginning by checking patient preferences for how much detail they want and calibrating disclosure depth to both patient readiness and clinical risk level—including lighter framing when urgency demands immediate action. Uncertainty should be communicated in operational terms: what is most likely, what remains unknown, what specific tests or timelines will resolve it, safety-net instructions, escalation triggers, and who will follow up—avoiding speculative open-ended differentials presented as equally probable. The clinician should invite questions, check understanding, and ensure the patient can use the information to participate in decisions without bearing the psychological burden of uncertainty alone.
integration_rationale: All three modifications shared overlapping demands—patient preference-checking, operationally concrete uncertainty framing, clear timelines and follow-up, and proportionality to risk—allowing full integration without contradiction. Stakeholder C's proportionality guardrail (lighter framing in urgent treatment contexts) was incorporated alongside Stakeholders A and B's patient-controlled pacing, as these are complementary rather than conflicting constraints.
